resources.string: Performs Back, Home, and Recents when an edge zone is swiped.
Enabled in Settings, but Android lost the binding after the last app update. Open Accessibility settings, toggle Ogesture off and back on.
Android only lets an accessibility service perform Back, Home, and Recents. Ogesture uses it for nothing else — it runs one of those actions when you swipe in from a screen edge.

Nothing is collected, stored off your phone, or shared with anyone. Ogesture has no internet permission, no ads, and no analytics. Your settings stay on this device and are deleted when you uninstall the app.
You can turn the service off at any time in Settings › Accessibility › Ogesture.
All set — flip the switch to start.
Edge gestures turned off: the accessibility service isn\'t running.
Edge gestures turned off: allow unrestricted battery usage.
Edge gestures turned off: they can\'t run right now.
Granted — the system won\'t sleep the gesture service.
Required. Without this, Android or your phone\'s battery manager can kill the gesture service in the background, so gestures can\'t run reliably.
Also open Settings › Battery › Background usage limits and make sure Ogesture is not in the \"Sleeping apps\" or \"Deep sleeping apps\" list.
Also enable the \"Autostart\" permission for Ogesture in your phone\'s settings (on Xiaomi: Security app › Permissions › Autostart). Without it, the gesture service can be killed in the background.
Swipe up from the bottom edge.
Swipe up from the bottom edge and hold.
Swipe inward from the left or right edge.
Adjust where Back, Home and Recents gestures can start.
Adjust where each gesture can start. Changes apply immediately.
How much of the side edge can start Back, measured upward from the bottom.
How far inward from the side edge a touch may start.
Pull back toward the side edge before lifting to cancel Back.
Home and Recents share the same bottom gesture region.
Width of the bottom area that can start Home or Recents.
How far above the bottom edge a touch may start.
Pull back down before lifting to cancel Home. It does not undo Recents after its hold action fires.
Turn Ogesture off inside apps that ignore gesture taps.

A few apps may ignore the touches on gesture areas for security or other reasons. In those apps a tap near a screen edge may not work. Swipes for Back, Home, and Recents still work fine.\n\nIf dead taps bother you in an app, add it here — Ogesture will stay off inside that app.
No apps added yet — gestures are on everywhere.
Optionally hide the OEM navigation buttons so Ogesture can fully replace them with gestures.

On some Xiaomi/HyperOS devices the system three-button navigation bar can come back even after you switched to gesture navigation. This optional watchdog keeps it hidden while Ogesture handles Back, Home and Recents.
Keeps the Xiaomi/HyperOS three-button navigation bar hidden while Ogesture handles Back, Home and Recents.
Not supported on this device. This option is for Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO devices running MIUI/HyperOS.
To let Ogesture hide the system navigation buttons, enable USB debugging on your phone, connect it to a computer with Android Platform Tools/ADB, and run this command once:
adb shell pm grant com.ogesture android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS

Root is not required. The command needs to be run only once after installation, unless the permission is lost due to uninstall/reinstall or similar. Ogesture uses this permission only for the optional system-navigation feature. When the option is disabled, Ogesture stops enforcing these system settings and restores the previous navigation state.
Turn Ogesture gestures on first — this option only hides the system buttons while Ogesture is actively providing navigation.
Everything runs locally on your device — no internet, no ads, no analytics. Settings stay on this phone and are deleted when you uninstall the app.
